verses.1: Five days later, the high priest Ananias came down with some elders and a certain orator named Tertullus, who stood before the governor to accuse Paul.
verses.2: Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, "We have had peace in many ways through you, and many improvements have come to this nation under your good governance.
verses.3: We, most excellent Felix, accept and give thanks for everything with the greatest gratitude.
verses.4: To avoid troubling you further, I beg you to hear us briefly with your kindness.
verses.5: For we have found this man to be a plague and someone stirring up rebellions among all the Jews, and he is the leader of the sect of the Nazarenes,
verses.6: who also tried to profane the temple, whom we have seized.
verses.8: From whom you, if you wish, can examine him yourself and find out all these things about which we accuse him."
verses.9: The Jews also joined in, confirming that these things were as he said.
verses.10: Paul, after the governor nodded to him to speak, replied, "I know, most excellent judge, that you have been a judge over this people for many years, and so I speak confidently in my own defense.
verses.11: You can know that for no more than twelve days have I been in Jerusalem, worshiping in the temple.
verses.12: And neither in the temple did I speak to anyone or cause a disturbance, nor in the synagogues nor in the city.
verses.13: And these men cannot stand before you to prove the things they now accuse me of.
verses.14: Yet I confess to you that according to the way they call a sect, I worship the God of our ancestors, believing everything that is written in the law and the prophets.
verses.15: I have hope in God, which these men also accept, that there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the unrighteous.
verses.16: In this I also strive to keep my conscience clear toward God and toward people at all times.
verses.17: After many years I have done charitable deeds for my people, giving offerings.
verses.18: Some of these I found in the temple, not with a crowd or with any commotion,
verses.19: but certain Jews from Asia, who should have been present before you and accused me if they had anything against me,
verses.20: let these men themselves speak what they found to be wrong when I was standing before the council,
verses.21: or about this one voice which I cried out among them, standing, 'I am on trial today about the resurrection of the dead.'
verses.22: Felix, who had more detailed knowledge of the Way, dismissed them, saying, "When the tribune Lysias comes down, I will decide these matters."
verses.23: He commanded the centurion to keep Paul under guard and to give him liberty, and not to hinder anyone from serving him.
verses.24: After some days, Felix arrived with his wife Drusilla, who was a Jewess, and sent for Paul and listened to him about the faith in Jesus.
verses.25: While Paul was speaking about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix was afraid and replied, "Go away for now, and when I have time, I will summon you."
verses.26: At the same time, he was hoping that money would be given to him by Paul, and so he sent for him more frequently and conversed with him.
verses.27: When a year had passed, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus, and Felix, wishing to gain favor with the Jews, left Paul in chains.

notes:
Notes
- v. 6: The phrase "ὃς καὶ τὸ ἱερὸν ἐπείρασεν βεβηλῶσαι" ("who also tried to profane the temple") is rendered as a charge against Paul. The verb ἐπείρασεν ("tried") is used in the sense of attempted or attempted to commit.
- v. 22: The reference to "the Way" (ἡ ὁδός) is a well-attested early Christian designation for the Christian movement. It is left untranslated to reflect its symbolic and specific usage.
- v. 25: "ἔμφοβος γενόμενος" ("was afraid") reflects the emotional reaction of Felix to Paul’s message, as the Greek suggests a visceral fear or unease.
- v. 26: "ἐλπίζων ὅτι χρήματα δοθήσεται αὐτῷ" ("hoping that money would be given to him") is interpreted as Felix's expectation that Paul might offer a bribe or gift.
raw:
[1] Five days later, the high priest Ananias came down with some elders and a certain orator named Tertullus, who stood before the governor to accuse Paul.  
[2] Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, "We have had peace in many ways through you, and many improvements have come to this nation under your good governance.  
[3] We, most excellent Felix, accept and give thanks for everything with the greatest gratitude.  
[4] To avoid troubling you further, I beg you to hear us briefly with your kindness.  
[5] For we have found this man to be a plague and someone stirring up rebellions among all the Jews, and he is the leader of the sect of the Nazarenes,  
[6] who also tried to profane the temple, whom we have seized.  
[8] From whom you, if you wish, can examine him yourself and find out all these things about which we accuse him."  
[9] The Jews also joined in, confirming that these things were as he said.  
[10] Paul, after the governor nodded to him to speak, replied, "I know, most excellent judge, that you have been a judge over this people for many years, and so I speak confidently in my own defense.  
[11] You can know that for no more than twelve days have I been in Jerusalem, worshiping in the temple.  
[12] And neither in the temple did I speak to anyone or cause a disturbance, nor in the synagogues nor in the city.  
[13] And these men cannot stand before you to prove the things they now accuse me of.  
[14] Yet I confess to you that according to the way they call a sect, I worship the God of our ancestors, believing everything that is written in the law and the prophets.  
[15] I have hope in God, which these men also accept, that there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the unrighteous.  
[16] In this I also strive to keep my conscience clear toward God and toward people at all times.  
[17] After many years I have done charitable deeds for my people, giving offerings.  
[18] Some of these I found in the temple, not with a crowd or with any commotion,  
[19] but certain Jews from Asia, who should have been present before you and accused me if they had anything against me,  
[20] let these men themselves speak what they found to be wrong when I was standing before the council,  
[21] or about this one voice which I cried out among them, standing, 'I am on trial today about the resurrection of the dead.'  
[22] Felix, who had more detailed knowledge of the Way, dismissed them, saying, "When the tribune Lysias comes down, I will decide these matters."  
[23] He commanded the centurion to keep Paul under guard and to give him liberty, and not to hinder anyone from serving him.  
[24] After some days, Felix arrived with his wife Drusilla, who was a Jewess, and sent for Paul and listened to him about the faith in Jesus.  
[25] While Paul was speaking about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix was afraid and replied, "Go away for now, and when I have time, I will summon you."  
[26] At the same time, he was hoping that money would be given to him by Paul, and so he sent for him more frequently and conversed with him.  
[27] When a year had passed, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus, and Felix, wishing to gain favor with the Jews, left Paul in chains.

- v. 6: The phrase "ὃς καὶ τὸ ἱερὸν ἐπείρασεν βεβηλῶσαι" ("who also tried to profane the temple") is rendered as a charge against Paul. The verb ἐπείρασεν ("tried") is used in the sense of attempted or attempted to commit.
- v. 22: The reference to "the Way" (ἡ ὁδός) is a well-attested early Christian designation for the Christian movement. It is left untranslated to reflect its symbolic and specific usage.
- v. 25: "ἔμφοβος γενόμενος" ("was afraid") reflects the emotional reaction of Felix to Paul’s message, as the Greek suggests a visceral fear or unease.
- v. 26: "ἐλπίζων ὅτι χρήματα δοθήσεται αὐτῷ" ("hoping that money would be given to him") is interpreted as Felix's expectation that Paul might offer a bribe or gift.
